To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the IRSWG reached a consensus on the definitions for choroid invasion and optic nerve invasion and the guidelines for the handling of the enucleated eye for a diagnosis of retinoblastomas.
the IRSWG has developed guidelines for the processing and evaluation of enucleated specimens with retinoblasotma to facilitate the diagnosis, staging, and risk stratification for clinical trials.
we reached consensus on the pathology guidelines to examine enucleated eyes in retinoblatoma and on the evaluation of prognostics risk factors in retinal blastoma.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of the molecular and cellular mechanisms that control the development of normal and neoplastic cells in the retina and optic nerve, and the identification of novel therapeutic targets for retinoblastomas.
the development of new and efficient methods for the treatment of cancer.

the development of an efficient, practical and feasible methodology for the examination of the enucleation specimens and evaluation of prognos-tic risk factors in the eyes of children with retinoblatoma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the guidelines and criteria for the examination of the enucleation specimen for the evaluation of prognostically important risk factors in retinal tumors have been reached.
the IRSWG has reached consensus on the definitions of choroidal invasion and optic nerve invasion, and the criteria for the processing and handling of enucleated specimens with retinobLASTOMA.
the IRSWG has reached consensus for the processing and evaluation of enucleated specimens with retinoblastic tumors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the IRSWG has developed a consensus document for a standardized pathology reporting system for enucleated eyes for clinical trials to be used in the treatment of retinoblastomas.
we have developed a set of guidelines for the handling of the enucleeated eyes for retinoblastomas and the reporting of the histopathologic findings.

the International Retinomblastoma Staging System Working Group (IRSSWG) reached consensus for the pathology guidelines for examination of enucleation eyes and evaluation of histologic prognostic factors in retinoma.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we should all use the same criteria to stage and classify retinoblastomas.
there is no one right way to handle an enucleated globe with retinoblasticoma.
there is a need to establish a standardized approach in the processing and handling of enucleated retinoblastomas to facilitate clinical research and the conduct of clinical trials.
